title: Versioning and SemVer
description: Master version ranges, prereleases, dist-tags, and lockfiles — and override transitive versions when a patch is needed.

data.text: Semantic versioning is a promise about compatibility. `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH` means breaking change, new feature, bug fix — and every range in your `package.json` is interpreted against that promise.

data.title: 0.x versions are a special case
data.text: Below 1.0.0, caret only allows patch updates (`^0.2.3` means `>=0.2.3 <0.3.0`). Many popular packages live in 0.x for years, so pin them deliberately.

data.title: Publish with the right version and dist-tag
data.code:
npm version patch        # 1.2.3 -> 1.2.4, creates a git tag
npm version minor        # 1.2.3 -> 1.3.0
npm version major        # 1.2.3 -> 2.0.0

npm publish --tag next   # prerelease channel: npm i pkg@next
npm dist-tag add pkg@1.2.3 latest

data.text: When a transitive dependency needs forcing
You cannot always wait for a parent package to release a fix. npm uses `overrides`, Yarn uses `resolutions`, and pnpm uses `pnpm.overrides` to pin a nested dependency from your own manifest.

Ranges describe what is *allowed*; the lockfile records what was *chosen*. Commit it, never edit it by hand, and let `npm audit` and `npm outdated` tell you when the chosen set is stale or vulnerable.

data.title: Inspect and update what the lockfile resolved
data.code:
npm ls minimist            # show every resolved copy
npm outdated               # which ranges are behind
git diff package-lock.json # review resolution changes in a PR

items.question: Should I use exact versions everywhere?
items.answer: No. Use caret for normal libraries to receive security patches, and exact versions for tools or packages with a history of breaking minor releases. Teams with very large dependency graphs sometimes pin exactly and rely on automated update PRs.

items.question: What if a library breaks SemVer?
items.answer: It happens. Pin the dependency to a known-good version, open an issue upstream, and add a regression test. Ranges are a promise, not a guarantee.

data.title: Key takeaways
points: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH encodes breaking, feature, and fix releases.
Caret allows minor updates; tilde allows patch updates; 0.x narrows caret.
overrides / resolutions / pnpm.overrides force transitive versions.
The lockfile turns an allowed range into a fixed, reproducible tree.
data.takeaway: Interviewers often ask "what does ^ do?" — follow up with what happens at 0.x and how you would force a transitive security patch.
